text:
We just finished moving our team's CI to a new hosted provider. Small team, so we assumed it would take a week. It took closer to three.

The migration itself was the easy part. Translating pipeline configs is tedious but mechanical. The hard part was finding everything the old setup did that nobody had written down, like a nightly cleanup job and a couple of environment variables someone set by hand years ago.

Then there was the buildbot dashboard. We kept it running in parallel "just in case," and it turned out half the team used it as their main way to check build status. Nobody thought of it as a feature until we talked about turning it off. We ended up putting together a simple status page to replace it.

My biggest takeaway: run both systems side by side longer than feels necessary. It caught more problems than any checklist did.

What's the most surprising thing your team discovered during a CI migration?

I didn't know the details of the dashboard story, so I guessed at it. If you tell me what actually happened, I'll rewrite that paragraph to match.
